name: t_tx_OP_y
title: Fast calculation of 'z <- x OP y' and 'z <- t(t(x) OP y)'

origin.description: Fast calculation of 'z <- t(t(x) OP y)', where OP can be +, -, *, and /. For + and *, na.rm = TRUE will drop missing values first.
origin.usage:
t_tx_OP_y(x, y, OP, xrows = NULL, xcols = NULL, yidxs = NULL,
  commute = FALSE, na.rm = FALSE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A numeric or logical NxK matrix.

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: A numeric or logical vector of length L.

arguments.name: OP
arguments.text: A character specifying which operator to use.

arguments.name: xrows, xcols
arguments.text: A vector indicating subset of rows (and/or columns) to operate over x. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: yidxs
arguments.text: A vector indicating subset of elements to operate over y. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: commute
arguments.text: If TRUE, t(y OP t(x)) is calculated, otherwise t(t(x) OP y).

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

origin.details: If na.rm = TRUE, missing values are dropped before applying the operator to each pair of values. This only applies to additions and multiplications. For subtractions and divisions, na.rm is ignored. y is recycled across each row, which is the same as adding it to the transpose and transposing back.
origin.value: A numeric NxK matrix. Integer x and y stay integer for +, -, and *, and division always returns double.
origin.example:
x <- matrix(c(1, 2, 3, NA, 5, 6), nrow = 3, ncol = 2)
y <- 1:3
t_tx_OP_y(x, y, OP = "+")

translation.description: Fast calculation of z = t(t(x) OP y), where OP can be +, -, *, and /. For + and *, na_rm True drops missing values first.
translation.usage: t_tx_OP_y(x, y, OP, xrows=None, xcols=None, yidxs=None, commute=False, na_rm=False)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A 2-d array whose axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns, matching the printed R matrix. Logical values are 0 and 1. Integer values stay on the integer path. Floating values are computed as float64.

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: A numeric or logical vector. It is recycled in row-major order, one row at a time. A 2-d y is read in column-major order before that recycling.

arguments.name: xrows
arguments.text: 1-based row subscripts. None selects every row. Zeros are dropped, negatives exclude, and a positive index past the matrix is an error.

arguments.name: xcols
arguments.text: 1-based column subscripts. None selects every column. The same rules as xrows apply.

arguments.name: yidxs
arguments.text: 1-based subscripts into y. None selects every element. A positive index past y becomes a missing value.

arguments.name: commute
arguments.text: If True, t(y OP t(x)) is calculated. This is commute.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, a missing operand is replaced by the other one for addition and multiplication. This is na.rm. Subtraction and division ignore it.

translation.details: The scan lives in the Rust crate xopy, ported from matrixStats src/x_OP_y.c with byRow TRUE. y is recycled along each row. The missing-value and integer-overflow rules match x_OP_y.
translation.value: An array of shape (N, K). Integer x and y return int32 for +, -, and *, and float64 for division. Any double operand returns float64.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.x_op_y import t_tx_OP_y

na = np.uint64(0x7FF00000000007A2).view(np.float64)
x = np.array([[1.0, na], [2.0, 5.0], [3.0, 6.0]])
t_tx_OP_y(x, np.array([1, 2, 3]), "+")
